level1.text: A $40\,\text{g}$ neodymium magnet falls in a vertical copper tube at a steady speed. How large is the braking force exerted on the magnet by the eddy currents?

A light copper ring hangs from a thread. The south pole of a bar magnet is pushed quickly towards the ring. Which pole appears on the side of the ring facing the magnet, and does the ring repel or attract the magnet?
level1.answer: A south pole appears on the side of the ring facing the magnet, and the ring repels the magnet.

level1.text: An eddy-current brake slows a $450\,\text{kg}$ roller-coaster car on a horizontal track from a speed of $22\,\text{m/s}$ to a speed of $6.0\,\text{m/s}$. Other resistances are ignored. How much energy is converted into internal energy of the copper plates of the brake? Give your answer in kilojoules.
A $25\,\text{g}$ magnet falls in a vertical aluminium tube at a steady speed of $0.30\,\text{m/s}$. At what rate does the internal energy of the tube increase? Give your answer in milliwatts.

Under the glass surface of an induction hob there is a coil carrying a rapidly alternating current. A steel pan on the hob heats up quickly, but the glass surface next to the pan stays cool. Why does the pan heat up but the glass does not?
level1.answer: The alternating magnetic field of the coil induces eddy currents in the electrically conducting base of the pan, and they heat it; glass does not conduct electricity, so no currents appear in it.

level2.text: A magnet of mass $20\,\text{g}$ is dropped into a vertical copper tube $1.50\,\text{m}$ long. It emerges from the lower end of the tube after $10\,\text{s}$ and falls at a steady speed for almost the whole distance. At what rate does the internal energy of the tube increase during the fall? Give your answer in milliwatts.

A closed coil has $200$ turns and a resistance of $15\,\Omega$. When a magnet is pushed into the coil, the magnetic flux through the coil increases steadily from zero to $3.0\,\text{mWb}$ in $0.20\,\text{s}$. How large is the induced current in the coil?

A $20\,\text{g}$ magnet falling in a copper tube experiences a braking force from eddy currents that is proportional to the speed of the magnet: $F_\text{j} = k v$, where $k = 1.3\,\tfrac{\text{N}\cdot\text{s}}{\text{m}}$. What final speed does the magnet settle at?

The eddy-current brake of a train exerts a braking force of $60\,\text{kN}$ on the train when the speed of the train is $250\,\text{km/h}$. At what rate does the brake convert the kinetic energy of the train into internal energy of the brake and the rail at this moment? Give your answer in megawatts.

level3.text: In a physics lesson a $20\,\text{g}$ magnet is dropped $50$ times in a row through a vertical copper tube $1.00\,\text{m}$ long. Each time it emerges from the lower end at a speed of $0.15\,\text{m/s}$. The mass of the tube is $0.35\,\text{kg}$, and the specific heat capacity of copper is $385\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}}$. By how much does the temperature of the tube rise if no heat is transferred to the surroundings?

A pendulum made of an aluminium plate swings between the poles of a strong horseshoe magnet. An intact plate stops after only a few swings. When deep slits are sawn into a plate of the same size so that it is comb-shaped, the plate swings between the poles for a long time. Explain the difference.
level3.answer: Large eddy currents appear in the intact plate between the poles; by Lenz's law they brake the motion and convert the mechanical energy of the pendulum into internal energy. The slits cut the current loops, so in the comb-shaped plate the currents and the braking remain small.

level3.text:
Two horizontal metal rails are $0.40\,\text{m}$ apart, and their ends are joined by a resistor with a resistance of $0.20\,\Omega$. In the region of the rails there is a vertical magnetic field with a magnetic flux density of $0.50\,\text{T}$.

A metal rod lying across the rails moves along them at a speed of $3.0\,\text{m/s}$. The resistance of the rails and the rod is ignored.

How large is the braking force that the magnetic field exerts on the rod?
